# img_resize — Image Resize & Compress CLI

- purpose: Resize and compress images (PNG/JPG/WebP/BMP/GIF/TIFF). Pure Rust, no network deps.
- version: 0.3.0
- language: Rust
- type: CLI binary
- supported-formats: PNG, JPEG, WebP, BMP, GIF, TIFF (input); PNG, JPEG (output)

## Command Syntax

```
img_resize r_resize <PATH> [-o <DIR>] [OPTIONS] [--json]
```

## Arguments

- `<PATH>`: Image file or directory path (required, positional)
- `-o, --out-dir <DIR>`: Write results into DIR instead of overwriting inputs (directory inputs flattened by file name). Not allowed with -c
- `-m, --max-pixel <SIZE>`: Max pixel on longest side, proportional scale (preserves aspect ratio)
- `--rw <WIDTH>`: Exact resize width (must pair with --rh)
- `--rh <HEIGHT>`: Exact resize height (must pair with --rw)
- `-c, --resize-config <FILE>`: YAML config for batch multi-size output (always PNG; paths from the YAML)
- `-j, --force-jpg`: Convert to JPG (quality 100) instead of resizing
- `--json`: One JSON envelope on stdout (global flag, any position)

## Resize Modes (mutually exclusive)

1. Proportional: `-m 800` — scale so max(width, height) <= 800px
2. Exact: `--rw 1920 --rh 1080` — resize to exact dimensions
3. Config file: `-c config.yaml` — generate multiple sizes per YAML spec

## YAML Config Format

```yaml
vec_size:
  - [1920, 1080]
  - [800, 600]
vec_f:
  - "output/large.png"
  - "output/small.png"
base_f: "/output/base/path"
```

## Examples

```bash
# Proportional scale, single file, written to out/
img_resize r_resize -m 800 image.jpg -o out/

# Exact resize
img_resize r_resize --rw 1920 --rh 1080 image.jpg

# Batch directory
img_resize r_resize -m 1024 images/

# JSON output for scripting
img_resize --json r_resize -m 800 image.jpg

# Convert to JPG
img_resize r_resize -m 800 -j image.png

# Multi-size via config
img_resize r_resize -c sizes.yaml image.png
```

## Notes

- Directory processing: recursively finds all image files, skips hidden dirs
- Output: overwrites original by default (proportional/exact mode); pass `-o/--out-dir` to keep inputs untouched
- With -m, images already within the limit are left unchanged (status "unchanged"; copied when -o is given)
- `tinyfy` subcommand disabled and hidden (OpenSSL/musl incompatibility)
- JSON data: {total, failed, results:[{file, output, status: success|unchanged|converted|skipped|failed, original_size, new_size, error}]}
- Exit codes: see Machine Call Contract (5 = some files failed)

## Build

```bash
cd img_resize && cargo build --release
```

## Machine Call Contract (r_lit CLI contract v1)

- spec: docs/cli-contract.md (repo root); implementation: crates/rlit_cli
- json: `--json` is global; stdout carries exactly one JSON envelope, also on failure; logs go to stderr
- envelope: {"contract":1, "ok", "tool":"img_resize", "version", "command", "data", "artifacts":[{"path","role","bytes","sha256"}], "error":null|{"code","kind","message"}, "warnings"?}
- exit_codes: 0 ok, 1 runtime, 2 usage, 3 input, 4 external, 5 partial (ok=false, data still complete)
- schema: `img_resize __schema` prints JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) per subcommand, with x-cli (argv mapping, io role), x-effects, x-env, x-stdin, x-note
- non_interactive: never prompts
- effects: r_resize=pure (only writes declared outputs; in-place unless --out-dir)
